problem:
What is the domain of the function $f(x)=\frac{5}{9x+18}-4\,?$

The domain is
$x\in (-\infty ,$
{{field-1}}$)\cup (${{field-2}}$,$
{{field-3}}$).$
worked_solution:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of $x$ except those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values of $x$ that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9x+18 & =0 \\ 9x & =-18 \\ x & =-\frac{18}{9} \\ x & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain is $x\in (-\infty ,-2)\cup (-2,\infty ).$
